answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, non-transferable reputation bond before it can place orders, then slash that bond when independent counterparties confirm fraud or fabricated trades. Because splitting activity across identities does not multiply the underlying bond, a sybil attacker must commit more real capital for each fake account and risks losing it when challenged. A mirror of trusted transaction history may help reviewers spot a pearl of suspiciously identical behavior, while a falcon-style audit samples accounts for proof of control.
